retail:pos: Everything hangs off the POS — sales records, inventory, and the audit trail the CRA expects.
retail:terminal: The thing that takes money. Never just one — when a terminal dies mid-rush, the spare keeps the line moving.
retail:station: The till itself — screen, printer, drawer and reader per lane. No station, no checkout.
retail:ecom: A second till that’s open 24/7. Skip only if you truly sell in-store only.
retail:acct: The CRA doesn’t accept shoeboxes — and clean books are what make a processing audit possible.
retail:loyalty: Repeat customers are cheaper than new ones. If your regulars come weekly, this pays for itself.
retail:signage: Nice behind the counter; nobody ever lost a sale for lack of a screen.
retail:selfcheckout: Saves labour at volume — but each kiosk is a capital project. Price it, don’t guess it.
restaurant:pos: Tickets, tables and payments live here. The restaurant runs on this.
restaurant:terminal: Takes the money — keep a spare. One dead terminal on a Saturday night is a dining room that can’t pay.
restaurant:kds: The kitchen stops shouting and tickets stop getting lost.
restaurant:kprinter: The KDS’s backup — when a screen dies mid-service, paper keeps the kitchen firing.
restaurant:station: Bar and host stations — where orders and payments actually happen.
restaurant:sched: Scheduling by gut costs a manager 10–15 hours a week; the software costs less than one wasted shift.
restaurant:payroll: Payday errors are how you lose good staff. Automate the math.
restaurant:acct: Food cost means nothing if the books are a mess.
restaurant:aiphone: Pays when you miss calls during rush — but at ~$399/mo, count your missed covers first.
restaurant:reserv: Worth it when no-shows cost you tables; overkill if your book is regulars who always show.
restaurant:tablets: Line-busting and tableside ordering — a speed play, not a necessity.
qsr:pos: Speed at the counter is the business. The POS is the counter.
qsr:terminal: Takes the money — keep a spare. A dead lone terminal is a line walking out the door.
qsr:station: The counter station — order in, payment out.
qsr:kds: The kitchen’s eyes. In quick-service, the KDS is the difference between 3-minute and 8-minute tickets.
qsr:kiosk: Throughput without counter staff — but each kiosk is a capital project. Price it properly.
qsr:menuboard: Looks sharp, changes prices in seconds. Earns its keep at 3+ screens.
qsr:tablets: Line-busting during rush — nice when the queue hits the door.
hotel:pms: The hotel doesn’t run without it — reservations, rooms, folios, night audit.
hotel:terminal: Front desk and outlets take cards around the clock — spares aren’t optional at an 11pm check-in.
hotel:station: Front-desk stations where guests check in, pay, and complain.
hotel:guestmsg: Answers ‘what’s the Wi-Fi password’ at 2am so your night auditor doesn’t have to.
grocery:pos: Lanes are the business. The POS keeps them moving.
grocery:terminal: Every lane needs one, plus a spare — a dead terminal closes a lane on a Sunday afternoon.
grocery:station: Each lane’s full kit — screen, scanner, scale, printer, drawer.
grocery:acct: Perishable shrink hides in messy books.
grocery:ecom: Curbside and delivery are table stakes now — price the picking labour honestly.
grocery:loyalty: Works when baskets are big and trips are weekly; a points program nobody checks is just a discount.
salon:booking: No-shows eat 15–30% of the book. This is the thing that fixes it.
salon:pos: Checkout, retail sales and the client record in one place.
salon:terminal: Takes the money — keep a spare. A dead terminal at 5pm Friday is a book of clients who can’t pay.
salon:station: The reception till — where rebooking and retail happen.
salon:payroll: Commission and chair-rental math gets old fast by hand.
salon:acct: Product retail and service revenue need separating.
salon:crm: Worth it when you’re ready to fill quiet Tuesdays; skip until the book is the problem.
*:drops: Every wired device needs a path back to the switch. No drop, no wire, no connection.
*:ap: Staff devices and guest Wi-Fi need coverage where the work happens — dead zones at the till are not an option.
*:switch: The thing everything plugs into. Size it for today plus the cameras you’ll add next year.
*:firewall: Keeps the card network away from guests and staff phones. Your PCI scope will thank you.
*:internet: No internet, no card payments, no cloud POS. This one isn’t a choice.
*:ups: A two-second power blip shouldn’t reboot your whole network mid-sale.
*:guestwifi: Nice for cafés and waiting areas; skip it where customers don’t linger.
*:bopc: For the books, ordering and everything you don’t want on the till — a refurb office PC does the job.
*:failover: When the internet dies, card payments die with it. Failover keeps the till taking cards.
restaurant:inventory: Shrink and food-cost creep eat margin quietly. Software ties inventory to sales; manual counts (4–6 manager hrs/month) work, they just cost your time.
qsr:inventory: Food-cost drift hides in manual counts. Software flags it daily; manual (4–6 manager hrs/month) is free in dollars, not in hours.
grocery:inventory: Fresh and high-theft SKUs need daily visibility. Software gives it; manual counts (4–6 manager hrs/month) lag behind.
retail:labelprinter: Shipping + shelf labels without hand-writing — a $160 DYMO pays for itself in a month of avoided label chaos.
grocery:labelprinter: Deli + shelf-edge labels print in seconds — no more hand-written price signs.
retail:custdisplay: Shows the total facing the customer — fewer 'how much was that?' disputes at the till.
qsr:custdisplay: Order-confirmation screen cuts 'that's not what I ordered' remakes.
grocery:custdisplay: Price transparency at the lane — fewer disputes, faster bagging.
retail:pinpad: A second payment point keeps the line moving when the main till is tied up.
restaurant:pinpad: A spare reader for the patio or events — cheap insurance at $59.
qsr:pinpad: Second payment point for rush hour — the line never stops for one reader.
grocery:pinpad: Express-lane backup reader — one dead PIN pad shouldn't close a lane.
retail:scanner: A fixed presentation scanner at the till beats aiming a handheld at every barcode.
grocery:scanner: In-counter scanners are built for belt speed; presentation scanners suit express lanes.
restaurant:handheld: Take orders tableside without running to a terminal — but each one is an $880 device to drop.
restaurant:mprinter: Print the bill tableside instead of walking back to the station.
qsr:mprinter: Line-busting receipts at the door — the queue keeps moving.
*:station: The till itself — screen, printer, drawer and reader assembled per lane. No station, no checkout.
